overall: The AG found the Council violated the Law by not responding to an executive session minutes request within 10 days, though it had posted the minutes; posting delay was not a violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council failed to properly respond to a February 2022 request for executive session minutes within 10 days.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we find that the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely respond to a request for executive session meeting minutes, when it posted the requested minutes online but did not respond to the requester.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council failed to publish requested executive session minutes on or shortly after February 15, when the matter discussed was finally resolved.
allegations.key_passage: Where the executive session minutes were posted online within approximately three weeks of the resolution of the matter, we find that the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law in this regard.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Council's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Council that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
